I do today what you won't, so I can do tomorrow what you can't

The hardest part of a challenge, resolution, job, project, anything really, isn't the beginning or the end, it's the middle.

Here we are, in the grind of things. We have our groove (hopefully) and now you're bored and ready to get back to regular life and try the next thing. That's ok, that's natural. Did you know most new years resolutions are abandoned by January 17? If you've made it this far you're stronger than most.

Here is where you begin building discipline. Character. Resolve. Here is where you really begin to complete something.

How do you keep that fire and resolution you made at the beginning of the year? Grit. Gumption. Control. Passion. Spite. FOCUS.

If you haven't started exercising, you are doing yourself a huge disservice. You don't need a gym membership or fancy gym equipment, push-ups, pull-ups, sit-ups, squats and running (if possible) is a total body workout and will wear you out. The beginning of week 3 is when you start to see results. That again is right where people begin to fail. Be better than you were yesterday

I always think about the quote I saw on the back of a t-shirt more than 10 years ago: "I do today what you won't, so I can do tomorrow what you can't"

We have already accomplished more than the average person by coming this far. These couple of weeks in the middle are the most boring, uneventful part. Don't let it get you. Clean out the reminders of who you were, to make room for who you are.
